tool.name: SpatialSequentialNumbering
tool.summary: Numbers features 1, 2, 3 ... in a spatial reading order (row bands left to right, serpentine rows, or a Hilbert curve) or by several sort fields with natural text sort, optionally restarting in every group, and writes the number (SEQ_NUM) and a formatted ID such as D1-0001 (SEQ_ID) to a copy of the input or, opt-in, to the input itself.

param.name: in_features
param.dialogReference: Features to number (layer selections and definition queries are honoured).

param.name: band_height_m
param.dialogReference: Height of one row band in metres (required for ROW_BANDS and SERPENTINE); the first band is centred on the topmost feature anchor (of each group with a Group Field). For a grid, the row spacing (cell height). An information message reports the rows the run found, and a warning says when Band Height cuts them; neither names a value to enter.

param.name: hilbert_order
param.dialogReference: Hilbert grid refinement k: the grid has 2^k cells per side, so a cell is extent side / 2^k (default 16, from 1 to 30). The run warns when many features share a cell and names a higher order.

param.name: sort_fields
param.dialogReference: Fields and directions (ASC or DESC) for the ATTRIBUTES order, most important first. Text is sorted naturally; nulls are last. Geometry, BLOB and raster fields cannot be chosen.

param.name: group_field
param.dialogReference: Optional field whose values form groups; numbering restarts in every group, and the bands of every group are centred on its own topmost anchor. Geometry, BLOB and raster fields cannot be chosen, and SEQ_NUM is refused (the numbers would replace the group values). A Date group appears in {group} with its time (2024-01-01 00:00:00).

param.name: format
param.dialogReference: Template of the ID text: {n} the number, {n:04d} the number zero padded to 4 places (a width of 1 to 99 digits; a minus sign takes one place: -005; numbers wider than the width are not cut), {group} the group value, {prefix} the prefix. Use {{ and }} for literal braces. Only zero padding is supported: {n:4d} (without the 0) is refused with a message that names {n:04d}. Default {n}.

param.name: prefix
param.dialogReference: Text inserted where the format has {prefix} (default empty).

param.name: id_field_name
param.dialogReference: Name of the text field that receives the formatted ID (default SEQ_ID). A new ID field is the longest ID written plus room for longer numbers in later runs (at least 50), measured as the output stores text: bytes in a shapefile (an Arabic letter takes 2; at most 254), UTF-16 units in a geodatabase. An existing field that is too narrow is refused; widen it with Alter Field. It must not be the Group Field or a Sort Field; an existing field whose values would change needs overwriting outputs allowed.

param.name: in_place
param.dialogReference: Unchecked (default): write a numbered copy to Output Features. Checked: add the fields to the input and write the numbers there, after making a backup copy.

param.name: out_features
param.dialogReference: New output feature class (required unless In Place is checked): the input fields plus SEQ_NUM, the ID field and SRC_OID (input ObjectIDs).

param.name: updated_features
param.dialogReference: The numbered features: the output copy, or the input when In Place is checked (derived).

tool.usage:
Each feature is represented by one anchor point: a point is itself, a multipoint the mean of its points, a line the point at half the length of its longest part, a polygon the pole of inaccessibility (the interior point farthest from the edges, found to 1% of its extent's diagonal) of its largest part. Anchors are computed in a metric coordinate system (the input's own system if it is projected, otherwise a UTM zone chosen from the data), so Band Height is in metres. With an unknown coordinate system the anchors stay in the data's own units: Band Height is used in those units (warning) and the run's messages give lengths in 'native units', not metres. Geographic data spanning more than 3 UTM zones is still banded in the one UTM zone of its centre (with a warning), so far from that zone the bands follow that zone's grid north, not the parallels; project such data first for true east-west rows.

Built-in alternatives: Sort with a spatial sort, Number Features and Number Features By Sector (Defense) need an Advanced licence, and none writes a formatted ID per group; this tool runs on any licence.

ROW_BANDS: horizontal bands of Band Height centred on the topmost anchor (the first band reaches half a Band Height above and below it; not a fixed origin; with a Group Field, on the topmost anchor of each group). For rows of features set Band Height to the row spacing (cell height): every row then lies in the middle of its own band, so noise, digitising or a polygon anchor that wanders inside a tall parcel moves it less than half a band. A larger value puts parts of two rows into one band (interleaved); a smaller value drifts against the rows and, on data that is not exact, cuts a row lower down. A point exactly on a band edge (within 0.05 mm) belongs to the lower band; left to right in each band. SERPENTINE: like ROW_BANDS but the direction alternates over the bands that hold features: the first occupied band runs left to right, the next occupied band right to left, and so on, so an empty band between two rows (a road, or a Band Height smaller than the row spacing) does not make two rows run the same way; with a Group Field the occupied bands are counted per group. HILBERT: order along a Hilbert curve over a 2^k x 2^k grid (k = Hilbert Order) laid over the square that holds the anchors, so a cell is extent side / 2^k wide (about 30 m for a 2,000 km extent at k = 16); this keeps neighbouring features close in the sequence. Features in one cell are in ObjectID order: the run warns when more than 1% of them share a cell with another location and names the Hilbert Order that separates them. ATTRIBUTES: sort fields with ASC/DESC; text sorts naturally (Lot 2 before Lot 10): runs of digits are compared as whole numbers, so text decimals and signs are not numbers (12.5 before 12.25, -5 before -10; use a numeric field for those); nulls are last. Ties are broken by ObjectID. With a Group Field, numbering restarts at Start in every group; a null group value forms its own group, shown as NULL in {group}. When two features get the same ID text (a text group value NULL next to empty group values, 1 next to '1', a format without {n}) the run warns that the IDs are not unique; IDs that repeat only because the numbering restarts per group and the format has no {group} are noted once as information. Features without geometry get no number in the spatial orders (warning); in a shapefile, which cannot store an empty number, their SEQ_NUM is 0 (warning).

Default: the numbers are computed on the input (a layer's selection and definition query are honoured; ties use the input's ObjectIDs) and a new feature class is written with the input's fields (types, lengths, aliases and domain names; a warning lists fields whose domain the output workspace does not have), SEQ_NUM, the ID field and SRC_OID with the input ObjectID (SRC_OID_1, ... when the input already has a SRC_OID field). Input fields whose names clash in a shapefile (names cut to 10 bytes (about 5 Arabic letters)) are renamed as Copy Features does (ROAD_NAME_, ROAD_NAM_1); a shapefile cannot store field aliases, so an info message gives each renamed field's full name. A new shapefile has its own integer Id field (left empty), so an input field called ID is copied as ID_1 with a message. FLOAT group values appear in {group} as stored (0.1). Its geometry is 2D (Z and M are not copied) and true curves are densified; subtypes, GlobalIDs and BLOB/raster fields are not copied. Use In Place to keep everything. In place (opt-in): a backup copy <name>_backupN is made next to the input first (the tool stops if that fails), the fields are added, and only the selected features of a layer are numbered, in one edit session. Features outside the layer's selection or definition query keep their existing numbers, so numbers can repeat; the tool warns when one of them already holds a number this run assigns (in the same group). If an unexpected error stops the edit, the edits are rolled back and the error names the backup copy and any fields already added (they stay on the input, empty). An existing numeric SEQ_NUM (Short, Long, BigInteger, Float or Double) and an existing text ID field are reused; a Short or Float SEQ_NUM is refused when this run's numbers do not fit it (Short -32,768 to 32,767; Float whole numbers up to 16,777,216), and a SEQ_NUM of another type is refused. Only rows whose values change are written. An information message says how many non-empty SEQ_NUM values this run replaces or empties. SEQ_NUM cannot be the Group Field (the numbers would replace the group values); as a Sort Field it is allowed (renumbering in the old order) and an information message says its values are replaced. ID Field Name: the Group Field or a Sort Field is refused (the IDs would replace the values the numbering is based on); an existing field whose non-empty values this run would change (in the copy or in place) is refused unless geoprocessing may overwrite outputs, and then a warning names the field and how many values are replaced, and how many are emptied (a feature without geometry gets no ID in the spatial orders). A layer with a join cannot be numbered in place (ArcGIS does not support an update cursor on a joined layer): the tool stops before the backup and the new fields; write a numbered copy instead, or remove the join first. If the ID Field Name is changed by the output workspace (a reserved word such as GROUP becomes GROUP_) the field gets the changed name and an info message says so. A not-a-number (NaN) value counts as empty: last in ATTRIBUTES, and the NULL group. An empty input (or a selection or definition query that hides everything) gives an empty output and a warning. Existing outputs are replaced only when geoprocessing is allowed to overwrite outputs.

Choosing Band Height: for ROW_BANDS and SERPENTINE the run looks for rows in the anchors' y values (tolerant of noise: the gaps between rows must be at least 3 times the gaps inside a row, and coordinates rounded to whole metres are not taken for rows 1 m apart; a few scattered features are not taken for rows either: with fewer than 20 anchors every row must hold 3 or more and be level, so a group of fewer than 6 features is never checked, and the run says how many groups that is). Parcels of different depths along one street are read as one row per street (their anchors stand side by side along x), and a staggered lattice can be read in two ways; a Band Height that fits either reading is not warned about. If it finds rows it reports how many and their median distance and warns when your Band Height cuts a row or puts two rows into one band; otherwise it reports the typical spacing, the square root of extent area per feature. These messages describe what was found; they do not choose Band Height for you, because the reading uses only the anchors' heights. Check the numbering on a map.

Blocks or districts whose rows are offset from each other (out of phase) are cut at Band Height = row spacing when they share one band origin: give each block its own group (Group Field); the run warns and says so. With a Group Field the rows are checked per group, and the run says how many groups lie in rows, how many of them Band Height cuts and how many do not lie in rows.

Not done: the tool does not poll for Cancel inside its loops. A stray feature above the top row shifts every band (bands are centred on the topmost anchor); the run warns only when the shifted bands cut the rows it found, and the warning then speaks of rows out of phase rather than of the stray feature. There is no rotation or azimuth option: bands are always horizontal in the coordinate system used, so rows tilted by even a few degrees are not read as rows (an information message, no warning) and are numbered in a zigzag across the tilt.
